description: RFC 2069 Digest from httpd 2.4's mod_auth_digest with AuthDigestQop none, in front of the gateway's audit endpoint: the challenge, curl's authorized request, the same request again at once and after the nonce's lifetime, and a wrong password.
client: curl in its own container on the server's network, computing Authorization itself (--digest), read from its --trace output; repeated requests are curl's exact bytes, sent again by scripts/record.mjs over a raw TCP socket from the host.
substitutions: The gateway's audit endpoint is documented behind Apache 1.3's mod_digest (RFC 2069). No maintained Apache 1.3 image exists; this is httpd 2.4.68's mod_auth_digest with AuthDigestQop none, which answers without qop, nc or cnonce the way RFC 2069 does. httpd 2.4.69 refuses AuthDigestQop none at startup, so 2.4.68 is the last 2.4 release that can stand in.
AuthDigestNonceLifetime is 3 seconds instead of the default 300, so the recording shows a stale nonce after a short wait.
The audit endpoint is this set's audit.cgi, a shell CGI that prints the gateway's pipe line for its one period.

descriptions: curl's first request, without credentials: the 401 challenge.
curl's second request, with the Authorization it computed from the challenge: the CGI's reply.

exchanges.name: replayed
exchanges.description: curl's authorized request sent again at once, inside the nonce's lifetime.

exchanges.name: stale
exchanges.description: curl's authorized request sent again after the nonce's three-second lifetime.

descriptions: curl's first request with a wrong password: the challenge again.
curl's response computed from a wrong password.
